mbm-0001.clue: The loudest part happens before the picture starts.
mbm-0001.quote: I bring my loose change to the silent movies. When the pianist plays the rain scene, I tip the coins into his jar. He makes thunder with his left hand.

mbm-0006.clue: We set one more place than we need.
mbm-0006.quote: A little green beetle crawled onto my camping plate. I let him finish my cucumber slice and borrowed the lid of the cook pot for dinner.

mbm-0011.clue: I got tired of losing my keys in the couch.
mbm-0011.quote: I crocheted a pocket for the arm of the sofa. It fits my keys exactly. My cat tested it with one paw and now it holds one paw.

mbm-0014.clue: My instrument takes up half the kitchen.
mbm-0014.quote: Our drummer got the flu, so I played the washboard at rehearsal. The wooden spoon left a dent on beat three. I keep hitting it because it sounds right.

mbm-0015.clue: I can run the last block with my eyes shut. I count the gates.
mbm-0015.quote: The orange cat on my route usually watches me from a fence. Yesterday she trotted beside me for three gates, stopped at the fourth and looked back like I’d missed my stop.

mbm-0016.clue: That cassette is exactly one side of sun.
mbm-0016.quote: I lie on the beach till the tape clicks. Last time the gulls worked out my routine. One had a foot on my sandwich before the chorus was over.

mbm-0017.clue: That triangle still has chalk on it.
mbm-0017.quote: I stitched the last scrap of my school uniform into a quilt for my old teacher. She found the chalk pocket in ten seconds. Teachers know where everything goes.

mbm-0019.clue: The little red square is where the train turns.
mbm-0019.quote: My nephew pushed a toy engine along the seams of my quilt. I had to unpick one whole corner so his train could get home.

mbm-0020.quote: We cut our quilt strips to match the marks on the kitchen doorframe. My sister’s tallest year leans sideways because she was standing on one foot.

mbm-0021.clue: The tickets are cheap if you carry the chairs.
mbm-0021.quote: Every summer we hang a sheet between the garage doors. The night the projector quit, my uncle finished the monster movie with a flashlight and a potato masher. Best ending all summer.

mbm-0023.quote: I ran out of white cloth halfway through my moon quilt. The other half is the sleeve of my first kitchen apron. Even after three washes the moon smells like vanilla.

mbm-0025.clue: I get asked for my autograph on paper napkins.
mbm-0025.quote: At the fair I finished a powdered doughnut without licking my lips. My cousin put a mirror in front of me. I’d grown a white moustache worthy of the mayor.

mbm-0028.clue: Hold this end while I look for the North Star.
mbm-0028.quote: The first night camping with my niece, she wanted curtains. We pegged a dish towel across the tent door. She pulled it open to announce the moon like it was the star of a play.

mbm-0029.quote: My first weight set came with a coffee tin full of bottle caps. I drop one in for every set. On a good morning you can hear the gym through the kitchen wall.

mbm-0031.clue: Listen for the lunch bell before you move.
mbm-0031.quote: The park clock chimes at noon. I thought for so long about one knight move that a pigeon settled on my shoe. I left the shoe exactly where it was and won barefoot.

mbm-0033.clue: That blue ribbon used to be in somebody’s hair.
mbm-0033.quote: The wind carried off our beach volleyball boundary tape. My sister lent us her hair ribbon for the last corner. It’s the only court where I’ve ever dived for a bow.

mbm-0034.clue: My walking stick has a dent like a spoon.
mbm-0034.quote: We reached the top with a whole jar of jam and nothing to spread it with. I carved the clean end of my walking stick flat. Best toast I’ve ever eaten on a mountain.

mbm-0035.clue: My best editor has no patience for chapter two.
mbm-0035.quote: I read my ghost story to my kid brother. He fell asleep just before the ghost knocked. I rewrote the sound as three taps on a fish tank. Now he stays up to hear what taps back.

mbm-0036.quote: We got fog on the way down. I could hear the loose pebbles on the little footbridge before I could see it. Now every time I cross I kick one gently to say hello.

mbm-0037.clue: The corncob square is my signature.
mbm-0037.quote: My quilting club made a picnic blanket with a different lunch on every square. I stitched butter on my ear of corn so thick you can feel it through your jeans.

mbm-0038.clue: Hold the radio up to the phone.
mbm-0038.quote: The first time our band came on the local station I called Mum and held the receiver to the speaker. She sang the second verse a beat ahead of us. She’d heard every rehearsal through the wall.

mbm-0039.clue: I wait for the other paddle.
mbm-0039.quote: A heron kept pace with my kayak all the way down the inlet. Every stroke I took, its shadow made one on the water. I finally stopped paddling to let it win.

mbm-0040.quote: I went looking for the famous statue and came back with a sketch of a bus stop wearing a woolly striped coat. Even the little timetable had a scarf.

mbm-0041.clue: My lucky pencil is about two inches long.
mbm-0041.quote: From under the open canopy the sunflower field looked like a yellow thumbprint. I sketched it in my logbook back on the ground. The instructor put his actual thumb beside it for scale.

mbm-0042.clue: A clean catch sounds like nothing.
mbm-0042.quote: I sewed three beanbags out of odd socks. Two land with a thump and the striped one lands with a squeak. You can tell how practice is going from the next room.
